headings.text: Lay out your integration as a Kustomize service
Developing the core rmapi against the cluster

blocks.html:
This page covers running your product integration API as a workload on the Kubernetes stack (pvarki/opendefence-platform, alpha). The stack is Kustomize-based: each service has a base/ plus overlays/<env>/. There is no miniwerk-driven **MW_PRODUCTS** registration — your integration is composed in by manifests. The manifest wiring is in Register your integration (Kubernetes); this page is about the toolchain and getting a local cluster running.

Platform scope: k8s (Kubernetes only). The compose aliases (rmlocal/rmdev), the local :5050 registry, and miniwerk's MW_PRODUCTS do not apply — see Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose) for the legacy stack.

Toolchain

The repo pins tools with mise and drives the cluster with Taskfile:

mise install   # install all pinned tools (helm, kind, kubectl, task, yq, zarf, ...)
mise trust     # trust the repo's local mise config

Once mise is installed it auto-selects the correct tool versions when you enter the project directory.

Spin up a local cluster

task up     # create a kind cluster and deploy all resources
task down   # tear the cluster down
task        # list all available tasks

task up runs cluster:create (kind, using kind-config.yaml), waits for nodes, then deploy:local. The deploy is phased with readiness gates (from taskfile.yaml): infra-phase1 (cnpg, cert-manager, external-secrets) → infra-phase2 (trust-manager) → monitoring → opendefense (the apps). Kustomizations that include Helm charts (traefik, trust-manager, external-secrets) are built with --enable-helm.

The core API runs as deployment/opendefense-rmapi in namespace opendefense-system.

Lay out your integration as a Kustomize service

Follow the repo's working contract (agents.md): add a new logical service as its own k8s/<service>/ folder with base/ + overlays/<env>/. Use the existing mtx service as the model.

k8s/<service>/
  base/
    kustomization.yaml
    resources/
      <service>.deployment.yaml      # your <short_name>rmapi container
      <service>.service.yaml
      ...
  overlays/
    local/
      kustomization.yaml             # namespace, images, ingress, certs
      <service>.namespace.yaml
      ...

Rules from agents.md:

  • Keep base/ environment-agnostic — core resources and placeholder image names only; no hostnames, certs, or registry/tag pins.
  • Put environment-specific data (images: overrides, IngressRoutes, Certificates, patches) in overlays/<env>/.
  • Every environment needs its own overlays/<env>/kustomization.yaml, and overlays reference ../../base.

Container shape (model: mtx)

The MediaMTX integration (k8s/mtx) runs the integration API (mtxrmapi) as a container alongside the product. Patterns to copy for your <short_name>rmapi container:

  • A healthcheck-backed startup/readiness/liveness probe on GET /api/v1/healthcheck (mtx uses container port 8005).
  • Mount the CA bundle at /ca_public from the opendefense-bundle ConfigMap.
  • Mount the shared rasenmaeher data at /pvarki (so get_manifest() can read /pvarki/kraftwerk-init.json).
  • A persistent data mount at /data/persistent.
  • For component UIs, an ui-files emptyDir shared with an nginx sidecar serving /ui/<short_name>.

Deploy your changes

After adding your overlay to the aggregator (see Register your integration (Kubernetes)), build and apply with the phased task flow rather than ad-hoc kubectl apply:

task deploy        # phased deploy of infra + apps with readiness gates
# or inspect a single overlay:
kubectl kustomize --enable-helm k8s/<service>/overlays/local

Developing the core rmapi against the cluster

To iterate on the core RASENMAEHER API itself against a running cluster, use mirrord from the rasenmaeher repo:

mirrord exec --steal --target-namespace opendefense-system \
  --target deployment/opendefense-rmapi -- bash -c \
  'JWT_PRIVKEY_PATH=./locadir/private/rm_jwtsign.key JWT_PUBKEY_PATH=./locadir/public \
   poetry run uvicorn --reload --factory rasenmaeher_api.web.application:get_app'
TODO: confirm whether a mirrord-style hot-reload flow is also documented for product integration APIs, or whether iterating means rebuilding the image and re-running task deploy.
